misconceptions.description: Assuming equilibrium means there are no forces acting at all
misconceptions.trigger: learner says a body in equilibrium has zero forces on it
misconceptions.feedback: Equilibrium means the vector sum of forces is zero. Individual forces can still be large as long as they balance each other.

misconceptions.description: Assuming cable tension always equals weight even for inclined cables
misconceptions.trigger: learner sets T = mg without resolving components for an angled cable
misconceptions.feedback: For an inclined cable, only the vertical component of tension balances weight. The full tension is usually larger than mg.

misconceptions.description: Losing track of positive and negative directions in force sums
misconceptions.trigger: learner adds all force magnitudes as positive values
misconceptions.feedback: Equilibrium equations are algebraic sums. Forces opposite the positive axis must carry negative signs.
